blocks.text:
Your first days are in Rio de Janeiro: getting to know the city, Sugar Loaf, the Old Town, Corcovado and a night at the Sambadrome. You then travel to the Búzios peninsula for 7 nights by the ocean, without a compulsory daily sightseeing programme. This route suits you if you want to see the famous Samba Schools Parade and still have plenty of time to relax. During Carnival, the city follows a different timetable, traffic arrangements change, and night transfers need careful planning. The main journeys in this programme fit together: your airport welcome, transfers, Rio tours, the visit to the Sambadrome and the onward transfer to Búzios. Over 12 days, you will see Rio from several perspectives. From Sugar Loaf, you can see Copacabana, Guanabara Bay, the islands and the bridge to Niterói. From Corcovado, the city spreads out below you between the ocean, forest and mountains. In the Old Town, churches, monasteries, the Metropolitan Cathedral and the historic façades of the central districts take the place of beaches and panoramic views. The main night of your trip is at the Sambadrome. Thousands of performers, huge floats, costumes, lights and the samba schools' percussion sections turn the parade into a performance lasting many hours. Afterwards, the pace changes: in Búzios, you can spend your days by the water, explore the beaches, take a boat trip or simply decide on your plans each morning.

**Group departure:** 5–16 February

## Why Carnival and Búzios are combined in one itinerary

The Carnival section takes up just the first 4 nights, so the trip gives you time beyond the celebrations. In Rio, you can explore the city before and after the Sambadrome: go up Sugar Loaf, walk through the Old Town, visit Corcovado and experience the city's everyday rhythm between the main events. Carnival is the highlight, with a full sightseeing programme around it. Logistics matter especially during the holiday. Traffic arrangements change, planning your own return is more difficult in the evening and at night, and a visit to the Sambadrome requires tickets and transfers arranged together in advance. Your airport welcome, tours, parade visit and onward transfer to Búzios are already organised in sequence. This saves you from arranging each leg separately during the busiest period. The Samba Schools Parade is a competition. Each school enters the avenue with its own theme, music, costumes, dancers and decorated floats. Judges assess several elements of the performance, while the percussion sections set the pace for the huge procession. From the stands, you experience a show in which music, light, movement and the audience's reactions continue for hours. After Rio, the pace changes completely. In Búzios, there is no compulsory daily programme. The peninsula has a variety of bays: some have calmer water, while others have stronger winds and waves. You can take a boat trip, explore the peninsula by buggy, try different beaches or spend a day without travelling anywhere. Seven nights on the coast give you time to recover after Carnival night and several days of sightseeing, with more than a brief beach stop before your flight.

### Rio before and after the main night

Carnival is part of your introduction to the city. Before the Sambadrome, you have time to go up Sugar Loaf and see Rio's bays, beaches and mountains. After the celebrations, the route takes you to Corcovado for a different panorama: Guanabara Bay, the Niterói Bridge, the Botanical Garden, the Maracanã Stadium and the coast lie below. The two main viewpoints therefore give you different views. The Old Town adds a third perspective. Colonial churches, monasteries, the Metropolitan Cathedral and historic façades show you another side of Rio alongside the floats and beaches. In the evening, you can choose a restaurant or a walk by the ocean on your own. Options include Fogo de Chão, overlooking Sugar Loaf, and, after Corcovado, the Marius seafood restaurant. Your first 4 nights bring together several different experiences: an ordinary city evening after arrival, a panoramic tour, Carnival night at the Sambadrome and a quieter day on Corcovado. The transfer to Búzios then marks a deliberate change of pace after the sightseeing.
